verdict.rationale: MoQ Relay authenticates connections via JWT and ships official client libraries (TypeScript @moq/watch, Rust, and FFI bindings), with a quick-start demo that starts a relay and opens a player. This is the product's own token-auth and SDK-connect path. However, the evidence never documents a server-side session-creation step, how to mint scoped JWTs, or a short end-to-end token-to-client flow, and broadcasts are auto-discovered rather than created as sessions. Missing for 10: server-side session/room creation API, documented scoped-token minting (claims, permissions, expiry), a concise server-to-client connect walkthrough using the token, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create a session from my server, mint a scoped join token, and connect a client with the official SDK in a short documented flow

citations.quote: Encrypted via TLS and authenticated via JWT.
Libraries for Rust (native) and TypeScript (web), plus FFI bindings for C, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Go, and Dart.
Subscribe to and render MoQ broadcasts, with an optional `<moq-watch>` UI.
The default demo starts a relay, publishes a test video, and opens the web player.
